title: Hybrid rate-probe and degradation orchestrator for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience sudden multi-tenant surges from noisy customers and synthetic load tests which break throughput guarantees and cause cascading latency spikes. Current admission logic is conservative (hard drops) or blindly queue-first which either wastes capacity or escalates latency for SLO-sensitive tenants.

Goal: Implement a hybrid 'rate-probe + staged degradation' orchestrator that blends small, low-latency rate probes with progressive queueing and targeted shedding. The orchestrator should: (1) probe available throughput for each tenant group without affecting global SLOs, (2) route requests into fast-path, queued slow-path, or shed sequences based on per-tenant contracts and current headroom, and (3) emit rich observability events for rollback and post-incident analysis.

Scope: Dedicated fleet routing component, admission policy DSL extension, new per-tenant circuit state, and console dashboards for incident response. Does not include dedicated autoscaler tuning (separate follow-up task) but will expose signals used by autoscaler.

Non-goals: Rewriting the serving runtime, changing kernel selection, or adding new hardware scheduling logic in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Implement rate-probe stage that sends sub-token microbursts to detect effective available throughput without increasing p99 latency beyond 5ms for protected tenants
Admission DSL supports staged decisions: FAST (pass-through), QUEUE (bounded FIFO per-tenant), SHELL (deferred execution with token refund), SHED (drop with informative error)
End-to-end tests simulate mixed tenant load and demonstrate <2% SLA violations under controlled surge scenarios compared to baseline
Console shows per-tenant headroom, probe success rate, queue depth, and shed count with retention for 30d
Playbook entries and rollback flags are published in Confluence and verified by SRE runbook review

design_decisions: Use small, frequent rate probes (10-50ms microbursts) instead of single large probes to reduce measurement bias
Prefer staged degradation (fast -> queue -> shell -> shed) to optimize for latency-sensitive tenants while preserving throughput SLAs
Keep probe sampling adaptive: reduce probe frequency during stable heavy load to avoid added noise
Queue implementation will be bounded by token budget per-tenant to prevent unbounded memory growth
Shell path returns 202 with retry-after semantics and a lightweight refund token to preserve billing fairness
tradeoffs_and_risks: Probing increases control-plane complexity and may add noise to latency signals if misconfigured
Bounded queues can still add tail latency; we mitigate with per-tenant priorities and fast demotion rules
Shell path introduces client complexity (retry semantics) that customers need to handle; requires clear SDK guidance
Adaptive probe tuning requires careful defaults to avoid oscillation between pass-through and shedding
False-positive probes could expose capacity as available and cause overcommit; conservative default probe sizes chosen to minimize this
